intent: Several agents side by side. Each card sums up its sub-agents; one card can open into its sub-agent tree while the others shrink to a compact column.
useWhen: monitor several running agents or orchestrators at once
show sub-agent progress, cost, and time per agent
point the person at a sub-agent that waits for their OK
doNotUseWhen: a plain table of jobs — DataTable

agents.note: { id, name, status: "idle" | "running" | "waiting" | "done" | "failed", cost, elapsed?, meta?, subAgents: { id, name, status: "queued" | "running" | "waiting" | "done" | "failed", elapsed?, cost? }[] }[]

expandedId.note: Open card. Others render compact beside it.

onExpandedChange.note: (id | null) => void. Without it cards do not open.

onReview.note: (agentId, subAgentId) => void. Review button for a waiting sub-agent.

totals.note: Fleet line under the cards. Default derived; "" hides it.

requirements: each card is an article named by its h3
the agent name is the open button (aria-expanded) and stretches over the card
collapse is a named button with aria-expanded=true
focus moves into the opened card and back to its card on close
status is text, not color alone; bars are aria-hidden next to a text legend
Review buttons name the sub-agent; an agent with status waiting shows the waiting sub-agent as a callout on its card
motion is transform and opacity only, off under prefers-reduced-motion

doNot: Do not invent a local AgentFleet, AgentGrid, or AgentCard
Do not color status without the text label
Do not use raw hex; waiting uses caution tokens
Do not nest interactive controls in the card besides Review
snippet: <AgentFleet agents={agents} expandedId={openId} onExpandedChange={setOpenId} onReview={(agentId, subId) => review(agentId, subId)} />
